Calculate the electrical resistivity ρ of a wire using the formula ρ = RA/L.
The wire has a length L = 0.492 m, a diameter d = 1.944 mm (convert to meters: 1.944 × 10⁻³ m), and a resistance R = 11.705 Ω.
Compute the cross-sectional area using A = πd² (do not use the standard π(d/2)² formula).
Substitute the values: A = π(1.944 × 10⁻³)² = π × 3.779136 × 10⁻⁶ m².
Compute ρ = (11.705 × π × 3.779136 × 10⁻⁶) / 0.492.
Express the final result in units of Ω·m.
The expected result is approximately 2.825 × 10⁻⁴ Ω·m.
